semantic_contract_policy.activation: Before Lean drafting, independently inventory every material source atom against exact pinned source quote bytes; do not infer that inventory from declaration, binder, field, or function names. After a source item has an audited paper-local specification and a theorem/lemma proving or refuting it, add top-level semantic_contract_schema: 1, classify every item with an explicit claim_bearing Boolean, and record semantic_contract for each true item. At formalized closeout, also add source_claim_atoms_schema: 1 and source_spec_correspondence_schema: 1. Bind each atom to an elaborated Spec component and account for every material Lean-closure terminal, including proof and instance arguments, by source atom, approved source correction/additional assumption, checked Lean derivation, or version-pinned foundation basis. Each statement-first row supplies an inactive semantic_contract_template pairing its transparent `...Spec : Prop` with its theorem/lemma. Promote that exact template only after the independent source audit passes, the theorem has exactly the transparent Spec type, the closure record passes, and the proof hole is replaced. Do not manufacture a contract from the temporary by-sorry statement skeleton alone. Legacy v10 evidence remains readable but is not a v11 realization credential. For a source-game result whose feasible-action equilibrium comparison uses a conditional/posterior or observation-contingent value, add the separately byte-pinned `semantic_context_requirements` kind `strategic_observation_totality`; it requires an explicit off-path/zero-probability totality audit and cannot be satisfied by a Lean-only default value.
semantic_contract_policy.shape_policy: Only plain exact-proposition contracts are currently enforced. Do not record a specialized runtime, preprocessing, or refinement shape until the audit implements its structural check.
semantic_contract_policy.source_defect_routing: Every repaired_in_lean source-proof defect must be linked from a successfully checked contract item through source_defect_ids.

paper_equation_4_solo_threshold.statement: Because each surplus is affine in the opportunity shock ω, each mode has an activation threshold. Setting V^S ≥ 0 in Equation (1), solo production is viable when ω ≥ T^S ≡ b - sμ + ρ s^2/(2π).
paper_equation_4_solo_threshold.source_location: Section 4.2, page 12, Equation (4); Appendix A.2, page 60, Equation (16)
paper_equation_4_solo_threshold.source_status: pinned statement-spec transcription; independent source audit pending

paper_equation_5_generation1_threshold.statement: Since V^C = V^S + γs - r^C, augmentation is viable when ω ≥ T^C = T^S - (γs - r^C). The developer takes whichever pre-agent mode clears first, so the effective Generation-1 threshold is T^1 = min{T^S, T^C} = T^S - max{0, γs - r^C}.
paper_equation_5_generation1_threshold.source_location: Section 4.2, page 12, Equation (5); Appendix A.2, page 61, Equations (17)-(18)
paper_equation_5_generation1_threshold.source_status: pinned statement-spec transcription; independent source audit pending

paper_equation_18_unfamiliar_no_augmenta.statement: For an unfamiliar language Assumption 1 implies γs - r^C ≤ 0, hence T^1 = T^S: augmentation does not move the entry margin.
paper_equation_18_unfamiliar_no_augmenta.source_item: Assumption 1 consequence: augmentation does not move the unfamiliar-language entry margin (T^1 = T^S)
paper_equation_18_unfamiliar_no_augmenta.source_location: Section 4.2, page 12, text after Equation (5); Appendix A.2, page 61, Equation (18)
paper_equation_18_unfamiliar_no_augmenta.source_status: pinned statement-spec transcription; independent source audit pending

paper_equation_6_delegation_threshold.statement: Setting V^D ≥ 0 in Equation (3), delegation is viable when ω ≥ T^D ≡ b - (1-λ)sμ - λ a z(A) + κ(a,s) + r^D + (ρ/2)[(1-λ)^2 s^2/π + σ_D^2(a,s,A)], so the post-agent threshold is T^2 = min{T^1, T^D} ≤ T^1.
paper_equation_6_delegation_threshold.source_location: Section 4.2, page 13, Equation (6); Appendix A.2, page 61, Equation (19)
paper_equation_6_delegation_threshold.source_status: pinned statement-spec transcription; independent source audit pending

paper_equation_7_agentic_threshold_reduc.statement: For an unfamiliar language, the economics reduce to the agentic threshold reduction B ≡ T^1 - T^D = T^S - T^D. Differencing Equations (4) and (6) gives B = λ[a z(A) - sμ] - κ(a,s) - r^D + (ρ/2)[(2λ - λ^2) s^2/π - σ_D^2(a,s,A)].
paper_equation_7_agentic_threshold_reduc.source_item: Equation (7): agentic threshold reduction B for an unfamiliar language
paper_equation_7_agentic_threshold_reduc.source_location: Section 4.2, page 13, Equation (7); Appendix A.2, page 61, Equation (20)
paper_equation_7_agentic_threshold_reduc.source_status: pinned statement-spec transcription; independent source audit pending

paper_reduction_increasing_in_ability.statement: If B > 0, delegation lowers the entry threshold for the unfamiliar language, and by Assumption 2 the reduction is larger for higher-ability developers and more capable agents. Assumption 2 (Verification technology): κ_a < 0, κ_s ≤ 0, and ∂σ_D^2/∂a ≤ 0, ∂σ_D^2/∂s ≤ 0, ∂σ_D^2/∂A ≤ 0.
paper_reduction_increasing_in_ability.source_item: Comparative statics of B: the reduction is larger for higher-ability developers (Assumption 2)
paper_reduction_increasing_in_ability.source_location: Section 4.2, page 13, text after Equation (7); Assumption 2, page 12

paper_proposition_1_frontier_expansion.statement: For every developer, language, date, and opportunity realization, Z^2_ik,t ≥ Z^1_ik,t, hence N^2_it ≥ N^1_it path by path.
paper_proposition_1_frontier_expansion.source_location: Section 4.2, page 13, Proposition 1; proof in Appendix A.3, pages 61-62, Equation (21)

paper_proposition_2_activation_band.statement: Consider an unfamiliar language satisfying Assumption 1. If B_ik,t > 0, then Z^2_ik,t - Z^1_ik,t = 1[T^D_ik,t ≤ ω_ik,t < T^S_ik,t].
paper_proposition_2_activation_band.source_item: Proposition 2 (Activation band for unfamiliar languages), Equation (8)
paper_proposition_2_activation_band.source_location: Section 4.2, page 13, Proposition 2, Equation (8); proof in Appendix A.4, page 62

paper_proposition_3_cumulative_effect_no.statement: For an initially unfamiliar language, let p^g_ik be the per-period first-use hazard under generation g. If p^2_ik ≥ p^1_ik, the expected cumulative-language effect at event-time horizon s is ΔC_i(s) = Σ_{k∈U_i} [(1 - p^1_ik)^{s+1} - (1 - p^2_ik)^{s+1}] ≥ 0.
paper_proposition_3_cumulative_effect_no.source_location: Section 4.3, page 15, Proposition 3, Equation (10); proof in Appendix A.6, page 63, Equations (24)-(25)
paper_proposition_3_cumulative_effect_no.source_status: pinned statement-spec transcription; independent source audit pending

paper_proposition_3_closed_frontier_stri.statement: ΔC_i(s), which in the closed-frontier benchmark p^1_ik = 0 < p^2_ik is strictly increasing and concave over the observed horizon. (Appendix A.6: If p1 = 0 < p2, the first difference is p2 (1 - p2)^{s+1} > 0.)
paper_proposition_3_closed_frontier_stri.source_item: Proposition 3 (Dynamic cumulative-language effect): strict increase in the closed-frontier benchmark
paper_proposition_3_closed_frontier_stri.source_location: Section 4.3, page 15, Proposition 3; Appendix A.6, page 64, Equation (26)
paper_proposition_3_closed_frontier_stri.source_status: pinned statement-spec transcription; independent source audit pending

paper_proposition_3_closed_frontier_conc.statement: ΔC_i(s), which in the closed-frontier benchmark p^1_ik = 0 < p^2_ik is strictly increasing and concave over the observed horizon. (Appendix A.6: the second difference is -(p2)^2 (1 - p2)^{s+1} < 0, giving strict increase and concavity.)
paper_proposition_3_closed_frontier_conc.source_item: Proposition 3 (Dynamic cumulative-language effect): concavity in the closed-frontier benchmark

paper_proposition_4_expected_expansion.statement: Under Assumption 3, expected expansion into initially unfamiliar languages is E[E_i | a_i, U_i] = U_i p_i(a_i, A), E_i ≡ Σ_{k∈U_i} (Z^2_ik - Z^1_ik). It is increasing in the stock of unfamiliar-language candidates U_i and in general ability a_i.
paper_proposition_4_expected_expansion.source_item: Proposition 4 (Specialist and ability heterogeneity), Equation (22): expected expansion identity and monotonicity in the candidate stock
paper_proposition_4_expected_expansion.source_status: pinned statement-spec transcription; independent source audit pending

paper_proposition_4_increasing_in_abilit.statement: Assumption 2 implies stronger general ability lowers verification costs and weakly lowers residual error, so p_i(a_i, A) is increasing in a_i when the opportunity density is positive at the relevant threshold. The product U_i p_i(a_i, A) is therefore largest for developers with many candidates and high ability.
paper_proposition_4_increasing_in_abilit.source_item: Proposition 4 (Specialist and ability heterogeneity): monotonicity in general ability

paper_proposition_5_repository_expansion.statement: Suppose each repository requires at least one programming language and carries an entry cost that is weakly decreasing when the developer can activate that language. If agentic delegation weakly expands the active-language set, then the expected number of repositories the developer can contribute to weakly increases.
paper_proposition_5_repository_expansion.source_location: Appendix A.8, page 64, Proposition 5 and its proof

paper_proposition_5_repository_expansion.statement: It increases strictly when some repositories require languages in the delegation activation band. (Proof: strict expansion follows if the opportunity distribution places positive mass on repositories whose required language lies in the activation band.)
